story.title: The Map Spread Open
story.text: Fan Ju told King Zhao: befriend the far states first, then deal with the near ones.
story.narration: Fan Ju came from Wei to Qin and was received by King Zhao. He spread the map open: if Qin wanted to move out, Han and Wei lay right across its door, while Qi, Chu and Yan were too far to reach — better to make friends with the far states first, and then give all its attention to the near ones.

story.title: One Step at a Time
story.text: Qin did it in that order and walked out of the Hangu Pass, step by step.
story.narration: King Zhao took Fan Ju's advice: first he sent envoys to befriend Qi, Chu and Yan in the distance, so that they would not step in; then he turned back and, from the nearest outward, settled the affairs of Han, Wei and Zhao one by one. Step by step, Qin walked out of the Hangu Pass.

keyMoment.question: Han and Wei block the door, and Qi and Chu are far away. Where do you start?

options.text: Befriend the far Qi and Chu first, then deal with the near states
Take the far Qi and Chu first
options.hint: Reaching across other people's land to the far side — what you take you cannot hold.

options.text: Push on both ends at once
options.hint: Pressing at both ends leaves neither end strong enough.

keyMoment.reveal: What you do first and what you do later matters — settle the near first, and befriend the far ones first.

misconceptions: It makes no difference who you move on first — they all have to be moved on
Befriending the far states is about having warmer friends out there
What is too far to reach simply has to be endured

quiz.question: Who did Fan Ju advise King Zhao to befriend first?
options: The far states: Qi, Chu and Yan
The near states: Han, Wei and Zhao
quiz.explanation: Befriend the far, attack the near: with the far states friendly, they will not step in to help the near ones.

quiz.question: Why does the Thirty-Six Stratagems say to take profit from the near?
options: Ground taken nearby joins up with yours and can be held
quiz.explanation: Profit is taken from the near and harm is kept far off — reach across someone else's land to the far side, and even what you take cannot be held.

quiz.question: Two things to do this weekend: a dictation test due tomorrow, and a poster due next week. Which first?
quiz.explanation: Do the nearest and most pressing thing first — just like befriend the far, attack the near.
